Q: How do you optimize context cost without discarding rare but decisive evidence?
A:
Optimizing context cost requires balancing financial expenditure, inference latency, and task accuracy without discarding rare, highly decisive evidence. A frequent anti-pattern is applying naive greedy top-K semantic similarity selection: in enterprise corpora, multiple chunks frequently repeat the identical high-level policy or background information, dominating top similarity scores while crowding out a critical, low-scoring exclusionary clause or legal exception. Context engineering must therefore move beyond simple token minimization toward value-density optimization.

Production architectures implement a multi-stage filtering and packing pipeline: (1) Deduplication and clustering: semantic embeddings are clustered to detect redundant passages, selecting only the highest-fidelity exemplar from each topical cluster; (2) Multi-condition knapsack packing: explicit rules reserve guaranteed token slots for negative constraints, temporal recency tags, and qualifying exception clauses before filling remaining budget with primary evidence; (3) Extractive span compression: sentence-level salience scoring extracts only the operative clauses and numerical tables from long documents rather than injecting entire 1,000-token chunks; and (4) Evaluation across edge-case slices: offline regression suites must benchmark supported-answer accuracy specifically against test queries where the correct answer hinges on rare qualifying clauses. A prompt with 50% fewer tokens that fails on 10% of critical exception queries is an operational failure.
Why: Three repeated positive clauses can outrank one longer exclusion. Keeping all three repetitions wastes budget and can produce an incorrect answer even though the selected text has high average relevance.
Risk: Summaries can omit negation, dates, units or attribution that changes the answer.
Trade: Optimize useful evidence per budget rather than only total token reduction.
Try: Compare full and compressed contexts on a case whose answer depends on one exception.
